name: getElementById()
description: Returns the single element whose id attribute matches the given string.
parameters: id — the value of the id attribute to match (without the # prefix).
returns: The matching Element, or null if no element has that id.
notes: Fastest selection method since ids are unique; only callable on document, not on other elements.

name: getElementsByClassName()
description: Returns all elements that have all of the given class names.
parameters: names — one or more space-separated class names.
returns: A live HTMLCollection of matching elements.
notes: The returned collection is live — it updates automatically as the DOM changes, which can cause bugs when iterating and mutating at the same time.

name: getElementsByTagName()
description: Returns all elements with the given tag name, such as all <li> or <div> elements.
parameters: tagName — the HTML tag name to match, or '*' for all elements.
returns: A live HTMLCollection of matching elements.
notes: Like getElementsByClassName(), the result is a live collection, not a static array.

name: querySelector()
description: Returns the first element that matches a CSS selector.
parameters: selectors — a valid CSS selector string.
returns: The first matching Element, or null if nothing matches.
notes: Supports any CSS selector, including combinators and pseudo-classes, unlike getElementById/getElementsByClassName.

name: querySelectorAll()
description: Returns all elements that match a CSS selector.
parameters: selectors — a valid CSS selector string.
returns: A static (non-live) NodeList of matching elements.
notes: The NodeList is static, so it won't reflect later DOM changes; supports forEach() directly but not map()/filter() without Array.from().

name: document.forms
description: Returns a collection of all <form> elements in the document, accessible by index or by name/id.
returns: A live HTMLCollection of form elements.

name: document.body
description: References the <body> element of the current document.

name: document.documentElement
description: References the root element of the document, i.e. the <html> element.
notes: Commonly used to toggle a class or attribute (e.g. a dark-mode class) at the root level.

name: Live vs static collections
description: getElementById()/getElementsByClassName()/getElementsByTagName() return live collections (HTMLCollection) that auto-update as the DOM changes, while querySelectorAll() returns a static NodeList captured at call time.
example:
const live = document.getElementsByClassName('item'); // updates automatically
const frozen = document.querySelectorAll('.item'); // snapshot, won't change
notes: Iterating and mutating a live collection in the same loop can silently skip elements — convert to an array first with Array.from() if needed.

name: document.querySelector vs getElementById
description: getElementById() only matches by id and is marginally faster, while querySelector() accepts any CSS selector but always returns only the first match. Prefer querySelector()/querySelectorAll() for flexibility unless selecting by id in a hot path.
